name: Highlands 40

alpha.desc: The alpha view highlights the front of the property, showing a single-story desert-tone residence with an attached or connected detached structure to the right, set back significantly from the road|A curved driveway loops from the street access point around to the front of the residence, providing vehicle access|Numerous juniper and scrub trees are distributed across the property surrounding the structures, which will limit responder sightlines and movement off the paved driveway surface|The terrain is relatively flat in the immediate building area with open desert scrubland extending outward.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, revealing the right elevation of the main residence and a detached structure positioned to its left rear|A small green lawn area and what appears to be a light-colored pool or patio surface are visible on the right side of the main structure|The paved driveway is visible curving around the right side of the building cluster, connecting to the front access|Juniper trees are scattered across the right yard, creating natural screening between the structures and the property boundary.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the main residence and detached structure clearly visible in the center of the parcel|A green lawn patch and a light-colored rectangular feature consistent with a pool or spa are visible at the rear of the residence|The road running along the top of the frame represents the street frontage, and the long curved driveway connecting the structures to that road is visible|The rear and side yards are open desert terrain with scattered juniper trees providing partial visual screening.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the property from the left side, with the main residence and attached or adjacent structure visible in the upper right portion of the frame|The curved driveway approach from the public road at the lower left is clearly visible, representing the single vehicle access route to the property|The left side of the property is open desert scrubland with scattered juniper trees and no secondary structures or access points visible|The road along the left edge of the frame runs at a slight grade relative to the property.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single curved driveway that connects to the public road and loops through the front of the site, providing the only vehicle access route to the residence. The long driveway approach and the set-back position of the structures from the road will require responders to travel a distance before reaching the building cluster. Scattered juniper trees throughout the property limit sightlines to the structures from the road and will restrict off-road movement for responders. A pool or spa feature is present at the rear of the residence and should be noted for nighttime or limited-visibility operations.
clarifications: Is the driveway surface paved or compacted gravel along its full length, and is it rated to support the weight of a fire apparatus or ambulance? Is there a gate or access control at the driveway entrance from the public road? Can the driveway loop accommodate a full turn for a ladder truck or engine without driving onto unpaved surfaces? What is the address marking visibility from the road at the driveway entrance? Is the light-colored rectangular feature at the rear of the residence a pool, spa, or patio surface?
